RESOLVED with live-verified evidence, not just documentation reading. The 'classic' endpoint (/aq/observation/latLong/current/) most training data/tutorials reference is being retired by EPA on 2026-09-30 -- found via a dated, merged pyairnow PR migrating for exactly this reason, confirmed directly against EPA's own official PDF notice (AirNowAPIUpdates2026June.pdf), then confirmed live with an actual test query.

Correct endpoint: GET https://www.airnowapi.org/aq/observation/current/ziplatlong/ (?format=application/json&latitude={lat}&longitude={lon}&API_KEY={key}). Response: JSON array, one object per pollutant: dateObserved, hourObserved (string 'HH:MM'), localTimeZone, reportingAreaName, siteID, siteName, parameterName, nowcastAQI, aqiCategoryName, reportingAgency, lookupBehavior, consideredMonitors, lookupBoundary. Error shape: {"WebServiceError":[{"Message":"..."}]}. Empty array = no data.

Implemented stale-while-revalidate + single-flight via Cache.get_stale(), Cache.try_acquire_refresh_lock() (DynamoDB conditional UpdateItem), and TTL alignment to the next boundary since epoch (cache.seconds_until_next_boundary()) rather than a rolling window. Two real concurrency bugs found and fixed via live testing under genuine thread/process concurrency (not just simulated-lock unit tests): (1) Cache.put() used PutItem which wiped the lock attribute early, letting a slower request acquire a fresh lock and redundantly re-fetch -- fixed by switching to UpdateItem touching only Data/FetchedAt/ExpiresAt. (2) A TOCTOU race between a request's own miss-check and its own lock-acquisition -- fixed by re-checking the cache immediately after winning the lock. Also fixed bin/run_local.py to use ThreadingHTTPServer instead of the single-connection HTTPServer, since the latter made it impossible to observe real concurrent-request behavior locally at all. Added the missing dynamodb:UpdateItem IAM permission to template.yaml. Verified live at 10 and 20 genuinely concurrent requests against real AirNow: exactly one AirNow call per batch each time. 57/57 tests pass, pylint 10.00/10, sam validate --lint clean.

This is deliberately the kind of test that would have caught the two real concurrency bugs found and fixed in q9r.15 (a PutItem-clears-the-lock race and a TOCTOU gap between miss-check and lock-acquisition), both of which were only actually caught via live testing against a real ThreadingHTTPServer, not by simulated-lock unit tests.

Reviewed. Accessibility (kSecAttrAccessibleAfterFirstUnlock, not deprecated/insecure .always) and sync (kSecAttrSynchronizable=true) were already correct from 10h.5. Found a real gap: original AppGroupCache.get() treated an expired entry as a miss but never deleted it, so stale entries accumulated forever, and since cleanup only fired reactively on a get() for that exact key, a never-revisited location would never get cleaned up. Fixed with two mechanisms: (1) expired entries deleted both reactively on get() and proactively across every entry on each put(). (2) hard cap on entry count (maxRetainedEntries=10), evicting oldest-by-fetchedAt when exceeded -- TTL alone only bounds age not count. Added SharedCacheStore.allKeys() so AppGroupCache can enumerate/sweep its own prefixed entries without touching a shared store's other data. File protection: verified against Apple's own Security Guide that macOS has no per-file Data Protection classes like iOS -- Class A is backed by the FileVault volume key on macOS, Class D is unsupported. No per-file protection-class API applies here; documented this conclusion in the doc comment rather than leaving it silently unaddressed. Verified against both the in-memory fake and real UserDefaults. 68/68 tests pass.

RefreshScheduler derives a stable per-install offset within the refresh interval (persisted via SharedCacheStore, so container app and widget see the same schedule) and computes the next refresh time on that install's interval-spaced schedule -- spreading load across installs instead of everyone waking at the top of the hour. Offset generated once and persisted, not regenerated per call. Found and fixed a real floating-point precision bug via testing: Date stores time relative to 2001 not 1970, so converting large 'seconds since 1970' values loses low-order precision, making a raw-Double 'strictly after now' check fail intermittently near computed boundaries. Root-caused with an isolated repro script, fixed by doing the strictly-after check and any bump entirely in Date's own domain rather than mixing pre/post-conversion Double representations. Verified with 30 consecutive runs of the specific test, then 3 full-suite runs. 75/75 tests pass via swift test.
